newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Creditors start discussing emergency loans to Kia.
newsitem.headline: Creditors start discussing emergency loans to Kia.

text.p: Creditor banks of South Korea's troubled Kia Group on Monday started discussing the size of emergency loans they would extend to four Kia affiliates, a senior Korea First Bank official said.
Korea First Bank's managing director Kwon Woo-ha told reporters that participating creditors were now reviewing rescue loan proposals by the bank and the nation's eighth largest conglomerate.
The bank, Kia's major creditor, offered 183.1 billion won in loans but the financially-troubled group had requested 515.9 billion won.

But those loans would be granted on the condition that Kia executives, including chairman Kim Sun-hong, resign and that the labour union agree in writing to reductions in wages and numbers of employees.
Unions had earlier agreed to those conditions but said they would retain the right to withdraw their agreement, if creditors forced executives to resign or allowed a third party to take over Kia.
Before the loan discussion, creditors unanimously agreed the bailout period for Kia would continue until September 29 without condition, Kwon said.
The bailout period means that Kia creditors would not call in loans, which should keep Kia from defaulting.
